column1: # kelsier keymap — docs/interface.md §6.
# One file, both implementations read it. Not generated from Go: bash has to
# work with no Go toolchain installed at all (install.sh's whole point), so a
# file "generated" by a binary that by definition might not exist would be
# the exact fork this table exists to prevent. Not hand-duplicated either —
# that was `kel cheat`, and it was wrong about five keys.
# Lives here, under cmd/kel-top/, not at the repo root: `go:embed` cannot
# reach outside its own package's directory (`//go:embed ../keymap.tsv` is a
# compile error, confirmed, not assumed). bash reaches this same physical
# file by repo root instead (see keymap_file() in bin/kel) — one file, two
# ways in, neither is a copy of the other.
# go_key is the Go surface's (kel-top's) single-shot key, chosen against the
# navigation keys that already exist there (j/k/g/G/s// /r/q/esc) — see the
# collision guard in test/kel-test.sh, which is what makes a repeat of the
# first `interface.md` draft (kill bound to k, k already meaning cursor-up)
# a test failure instead of a live bug. `enter` is the one deliberate
# exception: it currently matches no case in kel-top's Update() (a keypress
# with no effect), reserved for exactly the row `jump` occupies below.
# bash_key is the fzf board's OWN idiom, not a mirror of go_key — the board
# is a live type-to-filter picker, so bare letters go into the query, not to
# a binding (interface.md §2). "tab" and "prefix-m" name the MENU that reaches
# an action rather than a dedicated key: tab opens the board's per-agent
# action list (bin/kel: cmd_board_actions) where move/adopt/relaunch are not
# offered (they act on "whichever window I was invoked from", which only
# prefix m's version — cmd_here_actions — actually is); "ctrl-f" is the one
# key that opens the whole fleet-wide list (cmd_board_fleet_actions) and so
# is shared by five rows here on purpose (§5a: "ctrl-f mixes both, which is
# why it reads as too much and not enough simultaneously" — Phase 5 unmixes
# it). "-" marks an action Phase 1 records but the fallback does not reach
# yet: update and ls are plain `kel` subcommands with no board path today,
# and shutdown (#33) does not exist in bash at all yet.
# This phase wires neither column up. It is data, read by both sides and
# proven to agree (`--dump-keys` / `_dumpkeys`) — nothing renders differently.
